DESIGN NOTES / SEPTEMBER 2026

Behind
the threads.

A local story, a practical brief, and an invitation to make things together.

Independent pre-event concept · Not the official community website
01 / THE BRIEF

Make the community
feel like a community.

The September 29 AI Design Bake-Off asks small teams to redesign cvaiex.org using AI front-end design tools. The emphasis is visual design and user experience, using the existing community content as a starting point.

This concept was prepared in advance. It is a contribution to that conversation, not a claim to be work completed during the 45-minute session.

Read the original brief ↗
02 / THE LOCAL THREAD

From a textile history
to a shared future.

The Ix site’s textile history began in 1928. The mill closed in 1999; today the neighborhood is home to art, work, and community. Studio IX brings independent workers together and supports local artists through its gallery programming.

That connection suggested a visual language: luminous individual strands woven into a shared form. The artwork is an original AI-generated abstraction, not a photograph of the venue or an existing local artwork.

Ix history ↗Studio IX ↗Gallery & community ↗
03 / THE DECISIONS

Beautiful is a start.
Useful is the point.

  1. Put the next gathering within reach.

    The event’s date, time, venue, and Meetup link are easy to find. The schedule explains how the evening actually works.

  2. Give curiosity three ways in.

    Build, Learn, and Share turn the community’s existing mission into an interactive invitation. The connecting lines respond to the selected thread.

  3. Make the history specific.

    Recent events link to real source pages. The August joint session is correctly located at UVA, while June and July were at Studio IX.

  4. Design for the person with a phone.

    Touch-friendly interactions, a shareable QR code, and a downloadable calendar event support arriving and participating without a laptop.

  5. Keep access simple.

    Native links and disclosure controls work without a framework. The thread selector supports keyboard navigation. Motion respects reduced-motion preferences.

04 / THE PROCESS

Research. Make.
Try. Refine.

Built with Codex, using public-source research, original AI image generation, and custom HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. The website does not call an AI service when a visitor uses it.

The useful lesson: a precise brief and a real local reference give AI-assisted design something meaningful to work with. Visual polish still needs fact checking, careful interaction design, and testing on the screen people will actually use.

The site uses no member database, invented testimonials, or fabricated community statistics. Event content is a September 27, 2026 snapshot; the featured event changes to an archive label after it ends.

05 / THE RECEIPTS

A few threads
you can trace.

  • Original community website ↗Mission, activities, newcomer welcome, sponsor, and community links.
  • September 29 · AI Design Bake-Off ↗Brief, schedule, organizers, location, and participation guidance.

  • Original website repository ↗The community’s existing public website source.
06 / THE 60-SECOND TOUR

“I started with
the place.”

“The Ix neighborhood used to make textiles. Now it brings people and ideas together. So I built this redesign around a woven thread.

The home page tells you who this community is for and how to join the next meetup. Build, Learn, and Share give you three ways to explore. Each thread leads to something real: a gathering, a learning opportunity, or a conversation.

I used AI to help research, design, and build it, then checked the facts and the interactions. It works on a phone, because participating shouldn’t depend on owning a laptop.

This is my pre-event concept. I’d love to see which ideas we can take further together.”
